newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark not eyeing strategic partner.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark not eyeing strategic partner.

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark said on Wednesday it did not envisage a strategic partnership with another operator in connection with a planned sale of government shares in the firm.
"At present, we see no strategic partner to ally ourselves with in connection with a sale by the state of its stake in Tele Danmark," board chairman Knud Heinesen told Reuters in an interview.
There were rumours last June that British Telecom planned to take a stake in Tele Danmark, but these were dismissed by the Danish firm.

The Danish government said in the same month that it would sell all or part of its 51.73 percent stake in Tele Danmark, worth an estimated 23 billion crowns, but gave no date for the sale and promised a firm proposal this autumn.

"In my opinion, when the state finally surrenders its majority shareholding, it would be most natural for it to sell off its entire stake," Heinesen said, adding that Tele Danmark could well purchase some of its own stock.

"I cannot exclude the possibilty that we may buy some of the shares. We are of course interested in not remaining overcapitalised and would like to end up with a net capital which corresponds to our size," he said.
Tele Danmark in July appointed Goldman Sachs International to advise it on purchase options.
Heinesen warned that further redundancies would be necessary over and above the net staff reduction of 2,000 of its 16,500 employees to take place by mid-1998 announced last January.
"Given the present competitive business climate and today's staffing levels, we have to expect more cuts but it is difficult to say how many," he said.
"We have no concrete plans or figures at present, but redundancies are not over," he said.
Heinesen vowed that Tele Danmark would fight to keep its 50 percent share of the Danish mobile telephony market.
"Our assessment is still that the 50 percent mobile telephone market share we have today, is about right and we are prepared to fight to keep it," he said. --Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969658
